title: How Hearing Works and How Noise Damages It
description: How the ear turns sound into signals and why loud noise causes lasting damage, from the NIH and CDC.
narration: How does a wave of air become a sound you hear? Your ears carry out several steps that convert airborne sound waves into electrical signals. The auditory nerve then carries those signals to the brain. Loud noise, especially at work, can damage your hearing. Hearing loss caused by noise at work is permanent. Noise becomes hazardous once it reaches 85 A-weighted decibels. Tinnitus is the annoying sound of buzzing, rushing or ringing that seems to come from your ears or head. The good news is that work-related hearing loss can nearly always be prevented. Anyone exposed to hazardous noise at work should have a hearing test every year.
